name: Ellen Avila
life: “I still remember a child recasting my entire classroom in two minutes.” People around Tideline Market know Ellen by a small Saturday habit. Ellen picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I came to supervise the children and got cast as a lost umbrella.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a striped cotton shirt and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. Ellen has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Ellen listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Ellen can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Ellen can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To finish the scene in the role the children assigned.
family: Ada Murphy is Ellen’s first cousin once removed. Ellen asks before bringing somebody along. Ada can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *School after sixty*, Ada says, “I can do sums if I face a window. Facing the board takes me right back to the day I stopped going.”
connections: Greta Ray. The accidental cast member gets the camera put away for one private audience.

reactions.situation: A young actor asks the listener to stop the pocket play
reactions.response: Ellen lets the actor stop without calling the audience's attention to the interruption.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Ellen starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Ellen suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
